proof_audit.v13-c08-finite: Pass. Selected maximizing contracts induce a direct IC/IR menu only in the stated one-buyer commitment class. Pairwise IC gives monotonicity and adjacent bounds; telescoping plus monotonicity proves every pair. Minimal rents are componentwise smallest and feasible. The arbitrary-rent virtual identity subtracts both bottom rent and excess rents. Positive masses and strict quadratic convexity give unique quality allocation, while the stated tie rule is necessary for selected implementation. Bunching/cap optima have full-domain tangent certificates, including positive cap multipliers; no first-order-only or arbitrary ironing claim.
proof_audit.v13-c08-continuum: Pass. The pairwise inequalities bound every partition sum; monotone bounded quality makes the upper/lower gap at most Q times mesh. This proves the envelope including jumps, then integral bounds give sufficiency for all types and reports. IR reduces to bottom rent. Bounded quality and continuous positive density justify rent integration and the virtual-value expression. The uniform pointwise maximizer is monotone, hence globally optimal; strict concavity implies only almost-everywhere uniqueness. A changed top endpoint and its adjusted payment genuinely preserve IC and expected profit.
proof_audit.v13-c08-lotteries: Pass after the recorded integrability repair. Linear interim report utilities are preserved by means; convex supporting-line Jensen covers arbitrary bounded quality lotteries, with endpoint means degenerate. Per-report absolute payment integrability suffices for individual comparisons and finite types. The added joint measurability and population absolute-transfer integral justify continuum profit aggregation. Participation occurs before the draw and payment remains enforceable. The square-root example compares two fixed contracts only; the later-rejection exercise changes actual receipts and utilities.
proof_audit.v13-c08-signaling: Pass. Posterior-mean wage is explicitly imposed, not attributed to an unmodeled bidding game or finite sequential-existence theorem. Cross-type best responses prohibit reversed pure signals. Zero-signal and cross-signal deviations yield complete pure pooling/separating intervals, and low off-path beliefs prove sufficiency globally. Strict equilibrium-dominance excludes only a nonempty proper type set; the all-dominated exception is essential. Nonempty open intervals eliminate every pool and every excessive separating signal; full beliefs support least-cost separation. Uniqueness concerns the pure education outcome, not every belief or mixed/hybrid assessment.
proof_audit.v13-c08-productive: Pass. With both net marginal costs positive, the full pure intervals, strict deviation intervals and survival proof persist with the modified slopes. At kappa=1/3 the high maximal payoff equals its equilibrium payoff, so it is never strictly dominated. H belief is required above 9/2 but creates no strict gain; the complete piecewise schedule supports every finite h>=9/2. Pooling still has a strict high deviation. For kappa>1/3 a posterior-independent payoff lower bound grows without bound, ruling out every finite high best response. Productive output, private cost, wage and welfare are kept distinct.
